messages.subject: Time-varying Covariate error message
parts:
Hi all

I'm having a bit of trouble including a trap-specific time varying covariate in my model and am wondering if anyone can help. At first I though I was inputting the data incorrectly but now I'm unsure because I get the same error when I run the example from the help ('Time-varying Covariates'). 

Secr.fit produces the beta parameters and AIC etc, but not the fitted parameters and gives the error:

 "Error in secr.lpredictor(formula = models[[x]], newdata = newdata, indx = parindices[[x]],  :  model covariate blockt not found in 'newdata"

I'm unsure what this means as secr.fit seems to recognise 'blockt' in the model up until it tries to estimate the fitted parameters. 
Any ideas?

Many thanks
Chris

Curiously, the example in 'Time-varying Covariates' runs fine for me as given. It fails when I do not save the fitted model, but expect it to print immediately. Murray

messages.subject: Re: Time-varying Covariate error message
parts:
I got lazy and did not include time-varying covariates in the function makeNewData() that automatically generates the default 'newdata'. You can construct a suitable 'newdata' dataframe for yourself as shown.
Murray

messages.author: 9adc4986c319cfec
messages.subject: Re: Time-varying Covariate error message
parts:
Many thanks for your prompt response Murray.
I think I understand what you mean.... you are right, I hadn't run the predict function in the example and was just trying to run the model saved as 'fit.tvc2'. The the predict function in the example works fine! 

I'm having trouble applying this to my data though, so perhaps I should explain more fully what I'm trying to do.

I'm trying to run a secr model that includes temperature as a trap-specific, time-varying covariate (as I had traps open in different locations at 2 different times).
I've added the temperatures (rounded to the nearest even number, and padded out with 0s to the length of the longer period) to the trap object and identified these as time-varying using: timevaryingcov(trap)<-list(day = 1:9).

My model is: fit_day<-secr.fit(CH1, model = list(D~session, g0~day), trace = F)

Looking at the example it seems that the newdata data frame should contain the levels of the covariate (from example... newdata = data.frame(blockt = 1:2)). Is that correct? I'm not clear on exactly what the role of this data frame is.

This would mean that in my case newdata in the predict function should be something like:

predict(fit_day, newdata = data.frame(day = c(22,24,26,28)))

This appears to resolve the missing 'day' covariate as the error is now concerned about 'session': "Error in secr.lpredictor(formula = models[[x]], newdata = newdata, indx = parindices[[x]],  : 
  model covariate session not found in 'newdata'"

I had a crack at adding session to the newdata data frame but am unsure of how the two covariates should be combined (there are 13 sessions).

Thanks again for your help

Regards
Chris
